key_insight: The paper shows that good agent execution does not necessarily reveal which product improvement users would actually value, so decisions must be audited with decision-specific evidence rather than relying on task success alone.
engineering_relevance: For ML product teams, this suggests preserving structured decision inputs and building audits that explain unresolved choices before adding more telemetry or assuming model-generated reports are trustworthy.
method: Maps a declared observation channel and value contrast to compatible intervals and witness populations.
Runs a frozen experiment on two pinned model snapshots, plus an exploratory follow-up with supplied preferences.
Compares model-generated reports against a deterministic extractor and controlled multinomial simulations to separate ambiguity from identification limits.
evidence_signal: The study used 4,800 frozen requests, 2,400 follow-up calls, and 14,400 controlled simulations; all 36 conservative primary intervals remained unresolved, while the extractor resolved 7 of 9 comparisons without model calls.
watch_item: The approach can still leave many comparisons unresolved, and model-generated reports may introduce avoidable uncertainty if decision-relevant structure is not preserved.
paper_title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices
